{{nutritionsummary|1/12 of recipe (160 g)|12|715|461|51.2 g|34.6 g|33 mg|245 mg|58.2 g|3.2 g|44.5 g|5.4 g|4%|4%|10%|6%}}
'''Sticky toffee pudding (STP)''' is a rich, dense, gooey dessert originating from the United Kingdom that can now be found across the world. Often found on a [[wikipedia:Pub|pub]]'s menu, or in British or Commonwealth schools meals, this is a classic dessert that became popular in the 1970s.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.mcld.co.uk/recipes/#sticky-toffee-pudding |title= Sticky toffee pudding |author= Mcld (Wikibooks user) |date= 29 November 2008 |accessdate=19 July 2022}}</ref>

== Ingredients ==

=== Cake ===
* 1¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (250 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]/8.8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Self-rising Flour|self-raising flour]]
* ⅞ stick ({{convert|100|g|oz|disp=s|abbr=on}}) unsalted butter, room temperature
* 1 cup ({{convert|250|g|oz|disp=s|abbr=on}}) [[Cookbook:Superfine Sugar|caster sugar]]
* 2 large or 3 medium eggs
* 2½ cups ({{convert|250|g|oz|disp=s|abbr=on}}) [[Cookbook:Date|dates]] (without stones), finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 1¼ cups ({{convert|300|ml|USoz|disp=s|abbr=on}}) water
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|bicarbonate of soda]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] essence

=== Toffee sauce ===
* 1⅔ cups ({{convert|400|ml|USoz|disp=s|abbr=on}}) [[Cookbook:Cream|whipping cream]]
* ⅔ cup ({{convert|120|g|oz|disp=s|abbr=on}}) dark, soft [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
* 1 teaspoon vanilla essence
* 3 sticks ({{convert|375|g|oz|disp=s|abbr=on}}) unsalted butter

== Procedure ==

# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 180°C/360°F.
# [[Cookbook:Creaming|Cream]] together the butter, sugar and vanilla. You can do this by beating it in a bowl with a wooden spoon for about 5 minutes, taking care to break up the crystals and smooth the mixture out as much as possible. Or, do it using an electric [[Cookbook:Mixer|mixer]] if you prefer.
# Add the eggs one at a time, [[Cookbook:Beating|beating]] after you've added each egg.
# Fold in the flour.
# Bring the water to the [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] and add the dates. Add the bicarb and immediately take the pan off the heat. Let it cool slightly, then add to the [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]].
# Pour the batter into a greased [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|cake tin]]—make sure you use one with enough room for the cake to rise.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in the oven for 40 minutes, or until a [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewer]] inserted into the cake comes out clean.
# Remove from the oven and set aside to cool a little while you make the sauce
# Mix the sauce ingredients in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]. Heat gently, stirring often to make sure that the mixture doesn't separate, until it is a smooth sauce—don't allow it to bubble.
# Divide the cake into portions and poke holes all over the top with a skewer or chopstick.
# Pour the sauce over the top of the cake, making sure it gets in the holes. Serve with cream, custard, or ice cream.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Finely chopping the dates helps make a really gooey cake, but some people prefer to chop the dates roughly so that they're more obvious in the finished pudding.
